messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: Viscous friction depends primarily on velocity. Velocity determines the magnitude of this resistive force. This force acts opposite to the direction of motion. Motion in a fluid medium experiences such drag. Drag is proportional to the angular speed of the pendulum. The pendulum's amplitude decays over time due to energy loss. Energy loss is significant when damping is not negligible. Negligible damping allows for simple harmonic approximation. Approximation fails when the quality factor is low. Low quality factors indicate strong dissipative effects. Effects must be modeled accurately for precise period calculations. Calculations require including a torque term proportional to angular velocity.
